jobs.title: Research Staff, Voice AI Foundations [Remote]
jobs.description_text: THE OPPORTUNITY Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. THE ROLE As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Something has to decide which pages are worth indexing, which links are worth following, which pages say the same thing as pages we already have, what has gone stale, and what we should never have picked up. jobs.description_text: About the Team We are building the software that silicon chip designers should have had 20 years ago. Designing a chip today means stitching together a pile of desktop software, much of it decades old. We have a lot of respect for those tools, but in many ways they are behind. They've carried the industry this far, but we see enormous room to do better. For example: real version control, real collaboration, and interfaces that give you intuition rather than requiring it. We've concluded that we must build a lot of it from scratch. Studio is a fast, browser-based, multiplayer platform for designing and assembling whole chips. Figma plus GitHub, for silicon. The primary goal is simple: a user should never have to install anything or leave our app to take a chip from idea to finished design. Schematic capture, physical layout, and simulation, all in one place, end to end. Studio is one half of a bigger idea at Fab2: making chips should be fast. We build our own fab equipment for the same reason we build our own software, because the components for what we want don't exist yet. Studio is the design side of that, and we want to close the feedback loop between designing a chip and fabricating it, so the whole cycle gets faster instead of just one part. jobs.title: Software Architect - Tracking
jobs.description_text: This is the senior computer vision engineering authority for Hawk-Eye's tracking technology, and it is an individual contributor role. Our tracking sits underneath almost everything Hawk-Eye sells. Goal-line technology, semi-automated offside, electronic line calling, automated ball-strike. Live and post-game data. It runs across football, baseball, tennis, American football, ice hockey, cricket, basketball and rugby, on-premise, in the cloud and increasingly on edge devices, delivered by over 100 engineers in the Tracking and Automated Officiating value stream. You would be the person who decides how that is built. The role carries two hats. As Software Architect you own the software-level architectural design across tracking, auto-officiating and data delivery. As computer vision authority you lead the core domains: camera calibration, ball tracking, skeletal tracking, and the R&D that feeds them. It is a hands-on job. You set architecture for new tracking problems as they arrive, you safeguard the shared frameworks, and when a live delivery is at risk you are the escalation point who gets into the code. WHAT YOU WOULD OWN Architecture across the value stream. You are the lead architect for every tracking and auto-officiating product in T&AO. You set the initial architecture when a new tracking problem enters the business, run the Software Domain Owner model so shared libraries like calibration have named codeowners, and keep designs consistent across sports. jobs.description_text: You'll build the interfaces people use to run H's agents: the H Platform https://hcompany.ai/h-platform, where teams deploy an agent, follow it live and replay what it did step by step, and HoloTab https://hcompany.ai/holotab, our Chrome extension that controls the browser on its user's behalf. The work is mostly front end, in React and TypeScript, with changes to the Python APIs behind it when a feature calls for them. H builds agents that use a computer the way a person does, in the browser and on the desktop. WHAT YOU'LL OWN How people watch, steer and replay an agent while it acts on a computer, which has few established patterns yet. You'll decide how a live run appears and plays back, how live data gets to the screen, how a feature splits between front end and API, and which components become shared standards. We'll judge the work by what ships to users, by front-end quality held in CI, and by whether people can follow and control what an agent did. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING - Building the H Platform web app - Building and improving the HoloTab extension - Designing the live run view and replay - Changing the Python APIs behind a feature - Setting shared component patterns - Making long-running workflows easier for FDEs and customers to deploy and watch THE FIRST YEAR Within three months, a feature you built, API change included, is with users. jobs.description_text: ABOUT H: When we released Holo4 https://hcompany.ai/newsroom/holo4 on 28 September, we published every trajectory behind its public benchmark scores at trajectories.hcompany.ai http://trajectories.hcompany.ai. For OSWorld that's 369 desktop tasks, each run 3 times, with the steps, tokens and time of every attempt. This role builds and runs the evaluation framework that produces runs like these. H builds computer-use agents and the models behind them. Developers use them through a managed API https://hcompany.ai/newsroom/computer-use-agents-api, and our forward deployed engineers take them into enterprise workflows. WHAT THIS TEAM OWNS The evaluation framework: orchestration, runtimes and observability. Researchers and forward deployed engineers bring the benchmarks, across web apps, desktop applications and the command line. Your job is to make the framework that runs them reliable, fast and cheap, and to make adding a new one quick. Research uses the results to choose checkpoints and decide whether a model ships. That number should be between 100 and 200 soon, and the framework has to keep up. jobs.title: Legal Counsel - Commercial and AI
jobs.description_text: ABOUT H: Our agents act on computers for our customers, clicking through software and filling in fields, so our contracts have to answer some awkward questions. Who owns what an agent produces? Who answers when an output turns out to be wrong? Can customer data train our models? Our terms already take a position on all three, and they're public: read our general terms of service https://hcompany.ai/cgv and our data processing agreement https://hcompany.ai/dpa, both in French, under French law, and last updated in June 2026. This job is drafting and negotiating contracts like these, and keeping them current as the product and the law move. H builds computer-use agents for enterprises, from Paris. In July 2026 we launched Computer-use Agents https://hcompany.ai/newsroom/computer-use-agents-api, fully managed agents that take actions on computers. WHAT YOU OWN Our business teams bring in the deals. You'd write the paper behind them and lead the negotiation. When AI regulation or data protection law changes, you'd help work out what our contracts need to say now. You'd report to Julie Martinez, our General Counsel, who is also the data protection officer named in our DPA https://hcompany.ai/dpa. WHAT YOU'D BE DOING - Drafting and advising on a wide range of contracts, AI service agreements among them, with customers, partners and suppliers. - Working through the other side's mark-up. jobs.description_text: About Us: Grow Therapy is on a mission to serve as the trusted partner for therapists growing their practice, and patients accessing high-quality care. Powered by technology, we are a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Following the mass increase in depression and anxiety, the need for accessibility is more important than ever. To make our vision for mental healthcare a reality, we’re building a team of entrepreneurs and mission-driven go-getters. Since launching in February 2021, we’ve empowered more than ten thousand therapists and hundreds of thousands of clients across the country and insurance landscape. We’ve raised more than $178mm of funding from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, and others. The Opportunity: As Staff Product Manager for Grow's New Models & Markets team, you'll own new products and business offerings within Grow, particularly in the payor and EAP space. Behavioral health access is no longer the industry's biggest challenge — now payors (health insurers) are grappling with how to manage cost, quality, and outcomes at scale. As a Staff PM, you will be responsible for both deepening our partnerships with payors, as well as building an entirely new category of B2B offering for employers. jobs.title: Pilot Manufacturing Manager
jobs.description_text: Our first focus goal is to build better converters to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron Power's leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade. JOB OVERVIEW Heron Power's engineering organization is scaling from prototype builds to volume production, and this role owns that transition. We seek a builder, first and foremost — someone who thrives in a prototyping environment, gets energy from ambiguity and pioneering paths forward as processes take shape, and is genuinely at home on a factory floor. You'll lead the pilot build technician team and define the program-level process that turns engineering designs into buildable, repeatable, high-quality hardware — and you won't be afraid to get your hands dirty doing it. This is both a people-leadership role and a program-ownership role. Beyond hiring and developing the technician team, you lead the prototype program itself: build readiness, schedule, ramp-to-volume execution, and the handoff of manufacturing processes to the production plant. You will work daily across design engineering, EPMs, manufacturing engineering, supply chain, and quality to keep every build coordinated instead of executed in isolation. You are expected to operate with a “no surprises” standard — surfacing schedule, quality, and resourcing risk before it costs a build day, and be accountable to build status for each active program.
